newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bonds easier as market waits on jobs.
newsitem.headline: Australian bonds easier as market waits on jobs.

text.p: Australian bonds closed slightly lower in line with some overnight weakness in U.S. Treasuries, but traders classed the day as consolidative and said the market still had a supportive tone after the rally of the past week.

Trade was quiet, and undisturbed by the release of the Wallis report into the Australian financial system. Instead, traders were looking to Thursday's local labour force data for their next directional clues.
"I think we're just going to have a quiet one until the employment number tomorrow," one trader said. "We might get a bit of action out of that and the U.S. PPI on Friday."
Forecasts for the March labour force data centre on a rise of 13,500 and an unemployment rate of 8.7 percent. In February, employment fell 7,200 and the unemployment rate was 8.8 percent.

The Wallis report, which recommended allowing mergers between the four major banks and largest life insurance companies, as well as abolishing the blanket ban on foreign takeovers of banks, did not impact on the debt market.
Treasurer Peter Costello, when releasing the report, said at this time mergers between the four majors would not be allowed nor would foreign ownership go to substantial levels.

With the U.S. market facing a lack of data today, sentiment there is expected to retain its bearish tone, especially after concerns were raised that next week's inflation data could be higher than expected. ----------------------(SPREADS)---------------------------------

Afternoon softness sees initial narrowing in spreads across the board undone, although the long end does retain some of its gains. The more resilient performance of the long end sees the curves flatten on the day.
